persona.name: Nadine Roth
persona.education: Diploma in nursing (HF), further training in psychiatric and addiction nursing.
long_term_goals: Safe, well-documented withdrawal care for every patient.

occupation.title: Pflegefachperson (Entzugs- und Therapiestation)
occupation.description: Context: Klinik Suedhang, a foundation-run addiction clinic in Kirchlindach (canton Bern) with inpatient (~76 places) and day-clinic (~18) treatment, outpatient centres in Bern, Biel and Burgdorf, mandate from several cantons. Programme 'Mensch und Sucht' (qualified detox, then ~4 weeks psychotherapy; alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, medication). Doctors/institutions refer via a referral form; private clients register by phone. You care for patients during detox and therapy in shift work (early, late, night). You document Pflegeverlauf, observations on withdrawal symptoms, vital signs and medication administration, and write or dictate short Pflegeberichte and handover notes; you read doctors' and psychologists' reports to stay informed. You use a shared ward PC or a tablet in the corridor, hands often busy, sometimes in a hurry in a crisis. You need short, clear screens and a fast way to find the latest relevant report for a patient. TECH LITERACY: LOW. You are not technical and not ashamed of it. You are afraid of breaking something or losing a dictation. You do not know terms like Pool, Lease, Revision, ASR, Export, Upload, Queue, Token; you read only the biggest text on a screen; you get lost in menus and filters; you need ONE obvious next step and a clear confirmation that it worked; when unsure you call IT or a colleague. You mostly use the shared ward PC or a tablet.

persona.style: Practical, direct, friendly. Short sentences, concrete shift examples.

likes: Short voice notes instead of typing.
Big buttons usable with gloves or on a tablet.
dislikes: Logging in repeatedly on shared PCs.
Reports hard to find by patient/date.

beliefs: If a handover is unclear, patients are at risk.

general: Dictates a quick note at the end of a round.
Shares a ward PC with others.
Reads a report in 30 seconds before talking to a patient.
